stories.title: Social media making it harder for UK parents to raise families, survey finds
summary: Poll of parents of young children finds three-quarters think pressure from influencers has increased their anxietyParents of children aged five and under say pressure from social media influencers to be “the perfect parent” is making it harder to raise a family, according to a survey.Three-quarters (76%) of those who took part in the UK-wide poll agreed social media had increased anxiety around parenting, while three out of five (59%) complained of “impossible expectations” and “feeling judged”.

stories.title: Children in overcrowded homes get poorer GCSE results, study finds
summary: Researchers urge ministers to ensure young people in rented homes have space for a desk in their bedroomChildren who share a bedroom and lack a quiet place to study at home get worse GCSE results than their peers, according to a major report on how poor housing affects education.The research, carried out by leading academics at University College London for the Sutton Trust, a social mobility charity, urged UK ministers to ensure all young people in rented accommodation have space for a desk.

stories.title: Patrick Radden Keefe’s London Falling named Waterstones book of the year
summary: The word-of-mouth success of the journalist’s investigation into the death of a London teenager is ‘one of the defining features of the literary year’London Falling, Patrick Radden Keefe’s bestselling investigation into the mysterious death of a London teenager, has been named Waterstones book of the year.The book follows the parents of Zac Brettler, a 19-year-old who fell from the balcony of a luxury London apartment after pretending to be the son of a wealthy Russian oligarch, as they discover the murky, dangerous underworld of the city that their son had been drawn into.
